create.middle: --name, two --label, --network, two --env-file, four --env, the four --mount of the signed REQUEST, the signed image ID, python -I -B <the writer in the config root> and the REQUEST's writer argv

inspect.middle: one container name of this family or one 64-hex ID

logs.middle: exactly one 64-hex ID: the exited container of that window, identified (standard output only; the container's standard error goes to /dev/null with the CLI's)

remove.middle: 1 to 12 64-hex IDs: exited or never-started containers of this family, each identified and with its private receipt on the host when it ran

start.middle: exactly the 64-hex ID that create printed

stop.middle: exactly one 64-hex ID: the running container of that window, identified

directory.how: one mkdir relative to a held descriptor of its pinned parent, then identity, owner, mode and emptiness proved through a descriptor, fsync of the directory and of its parent

file.how: exclusive temporary, unbuffered writes, fsync, exact metadata, link to the final name (a link never replaces anything), fsync of the directory, removal of the temporary once its identity is proved, fsync of the directory

never: removal of anything but the temporary this run created and proved by identity
a write into the manifests directory, the capacity tree, the journal or the data directory by this process
a bind source not controlled by root alone other than the named read-only data volume
a read of the data volume other than the release file
the manifest hash or the symbol count in a receipt
an existing file overwritten, renamed, chmodded, chowned or removed
a container that is not this family's
scope.statement: The capacity-day window of epoch R2D2-V2-SHADOW-2026-10-05, one signed mode per request. LAUNCH: docker create (no --rm, --restart no, --pull never, --init, --user 0:0, --read-only, --cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges) and docker start of one container named c3po-k12-<yyyymmdd>-w<index>, labelled with this request and with the documents tool REQUEST it carries byte for byte, running python -I -B on the writer delivered by hash in /var/lib/c3po-capacity/config with that REQUEST's argv, network, two environment files and four binds (/mnt/day-d-data at /app/day-d-data, the journal and /var/lib/c3po-capacity read-only, /etc/c3po-bar/manifests read-write), every bind source and every ancestor of it controlled by root alone (uid 0, gid 0, no group or other write, no setgid, no link) except the named read-only data volume (Codex #429 5986698996: ancestors root-controlled, a mount point, the release directory root 0700, the release file hashed against the REQUEST before the create and again after the start); the container parks until its view. PERSIST: docker logs (no follow, no tail; QUICK class: bounded in seconds and bytes) of that exited container, identified by its ID, name and two labels, with a known exit code and not OOM-killed; the output must be exactly one complete writer receipt of this day and of a publish run, consistent with the exit code, or nothing is written; that receipt and the exit state go into one new private file (root:root 0600, exclusive creation, fsync, read back) in /var/lib/c3po-reader/capacity-receipts. STOP: docker stop of that running container before its view. REMOVE: docker rm without -f or -v of exited or never-started containers of this family whose private receipt is on the host or which ended by a stop before their view. A container is acted on only after its name, labels, image, argv and binds were read and found to be this family's. Nothing is written into the manifests directory, the capacity tree, the journal or the data directory by this process; no environment is printed; the manifest hash and the symbol count never leave the host.
